name_en: Decchi yokan — bamboo-leaf-wrapped azuki yokan thickened with flour
summary_ja: 小豆こしあんに小麦粉を混ぜて竹の皮で包んで蒸した素朴な羊羹。海のない近江では寒天が手に入りにくく、代わりに小麦粉でつないだといわれ、竹の香りともちもちとした食感が持ち味とされる。
summary_en: A simple steamed yokan made by mixing sweet azuki paste with flour and wrapping it in bamboo sheath. Landlocked Omi had little access to agar, so flour was used as a binder instead, giving the confection its chewy texture and faint bamboo aroma.

name_en: Kofuku mame — griddled disks of roasted soybeans and flour
summary_ja: 煎った大豆を小麦粉の生地に混ぜ、円盤状に焼いた素朴なおやつ。米どころの滋賀では米粉でもつくられ、甘いおやつが少なかった時代に農作業の合間の一服として食べられてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Roasted soybeans are folded into a wheat-flour batter and griddled into flat discs. In rice-growing Shiga the batter is sometimes made with rice flour instead, and the humble snack was traditionally eaten during breaks from farm work.

name_en: Oae dango — rice-flour dumplings wrapped in tofu-vegetable shira-ae
summary_ja: 米粉でつくった団子を、人参やしいたけ、こんにゃく、豆腐であえた白和えで包み込んだ守山・野洲地域の料理。お茶うけにもなる素朴な甘さで、主に法事の席で供されてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Rice-flour dumplings are wrapped in a shira-ae dressing of tofu mashed with carrot, shiitake, and greens. Mildly sweet enough to serve alongside tea, the dish from the Moriyama and Yasu area is traditionally made for Buddhist memorial gatherings.
source_title: おあえ団子 滋賀県
